rows: Roughly one in four to one in five interns receive a pre-placement offer. This is the number to anchor your expectations to, not the exceptional cases you hear about.
Some internship batches convert only one in ten interns. A low conversion rate is not always a red flag on its own, check headcount growth and team budget before reading it as rejection.

Large, well-funded tech employers running structured summer internship programs report conversion in this range because the internship functions as an extended, paid interview for a role that already has budget.

items.heading: IT Treats "Do an Internship
items.text: It treats "do an internship first" as universal advice, without checking whether the specific internship on offer has any real structure behind it.

items.heading: IT Skips the Actual Ppo
items.text: It skips the actual PPO conversion math, leaving people to assume an internship is a near-guaranteed path to a job when it converts roughly one time in four or five.

items.heading: IT Rarely Explains That Internships
items.text: It rarely explains that internships sit largely outside India's formal labour protections, so the responsibility to check terms falls on the intern, not on assumed regulation.

items.heading: IT Frames a Full
items.text: It frames a full-time offer as automatically "playing it safe," ignoring cases where the offer itself is weak and a strong internship would build more long-term value.
